findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will crash when instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from a concrete DetectorHandler subclass (with an implemented evaluate returning []) to a bare subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), none of which MetricAlertDetectorHandler implements. Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py line 86) calls group_type.detector_handler(self), so any attempt to process a Detector of type MetricAlertFire will now raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ..., whereas before this PR it worked. Either implement the abstract methods or keep the class off StatefulDetectorHandler until it is ready.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate reads 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult', but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. This is misleading for anyone implementing or consuming the new signature introduced by this PR.

findings.title: No validation that dict keys match each result's group_key
findings.body: With the return type changed from a list to a dict keyed by group key, process_detectors now blindly trusts handler-provided dict keys (detector_results.values()) and dropped the old duplicate/mismatch logging entirely. A custom DetectorHandler.evaluate that returns {key_a: result_with_group_key_b} would produce occurrences whose group_key doesn't match the key under which downstream consumers (results.append((detector, detector_results))) expect to find them, silently corrupting group-keyed lookups. A cheap consistency check (or building the dict from result.group_key server-side, as StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate does) would prevent this.
